key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents autonomously discover and train turbulence closures by combining LLM-guided model design with gradients from differentiable CFD.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce manual effort in developing turbulence closures tailored to target flow statistics.
method: Use a multi-agent LLM system to propose analytical, neural, or hybrid closure forms.
Embed closures and objectives in a GPU-native differentiable CFD solver and validate gradient paths.
Use simulation feedback and truncated-horizon gradients to optimize parameters and revise proposals.
evidence_signal: Tests span dissipation laws and subgrid-scale closures in 2D turbulence and wall models for 3D channel-flow LES; gradient-based training recovers reference coefficients not reached by forward evaluation alone within the same budget.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the demonstrated flows remains unestablished, and chaotic dynamics require careful selection of gradient truncation horizons.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
